stimulus.source_note: Original secondary passage written for this question, stating the argument the questions evaluate.
stimulus.text: A historian argues that the Columbian Exchange was an exchange of goods between the Eastern and Western Hemispheres that spread prosperity to people on both sides of the Atlantic.

stem: A historian argues that the Columbian Exchange was an exchange of goods between the Eastern and Western Hemispheres that spread prosperity to people on both sides of the Atlantic. Which response to this argument is most defensible?

options.text: Goods moved both ways, but Native peoples bore the epidemics and forced labor while Europeans gained most.
Judged by modern standards of consent and free trade, the transfer was voluntary exchange on both sides.
Potatoes transformed European diets and fed population growth, proving the exchange raised living standards everywhere.
Disease alone caused the collapse of Native populations, so the only harm was a biological accident no one intended.

instruction: Pick one option from the stimulus and stem only. Do not open the question file.
